words.enDefinition: An urgent message warning people about an emergency.

examples.en: The emergency alert reached several students while they were waiting outside the lecture hall.
examples.zh: 几名学生在阶梯教室外等候时收到了「紧急警报」。

examples.en: My roommate noticed the emergency alert on her phone before I checked my email.
examples.zh: 我还没查看邮件，室友就已经看到了手机上的「紧急警报」。

words.enDefinition: A system that sends a message to many people through one or more channels.

examples.en: The university tested its mass notification system during the first week of the semester.
examples.zh: 大学在开学第一周测试了「群体通知系统」。

examples.en: One announcement from the mass notification system appeared on both phones and library computers.
examples.zh: 有一条「群体通知系统」发出的消息同时出现在手机和图书馆电脑上。

collocations: messages from the mass notification system

words.enDefinition: A warning sent as a text message to a mobile phone.

examples.en: I got a text alert about the library closure on the way to class.
examples.zh: 我去上课的路上收到一条图书馆关闭的「短信警报」。

examples.en: The text alert named the closed building, and the email gave us a longer explanation.
examples.zh: 「短信警报」写明了关闭楼宇的名称，邮件则提供了更详细的说明。

words.enDefinition: An outdoor device that produces a loud warning sound across part of a campus.

examples.en: We heard the campus siren from the bus stop during the scheduled test today.
examples.zh: 在今天的例行测试中，我们在公交站听见了「校园警报器」。

examples.en: The notice explained which hours the campus siren might be audible near residence halls.
examples.zh: 通知说明了宿舍楼附近在哪些时段可能听见「校园警报器」。

words.enDefinition: A warning or update announced to a wide audience through a broadcast channel.

examples.en: The emergency broadcast interrupted the music playing over the speakers in the student union.
examples.zh: 「紧急广播」打断了学生中心扬声器正在播放的音乐。

examples.en: I could hear the emergency broadcast from the courtyard even with the lobby doors closed.
examples.zh: 即使大厅的门关着，我在庭院里也能听见「紧急广播」。

collocations: an emergency broadcast over the speakers

words.enDefinition: A microphone and speaker system used to make announcements throughout a place.

examples.en: The announcement came over the public address system just as our workshop was ending.
examples.zh: 研讨活动将要结束时，「公共广播系统」播出了一条通知。

examples.en: Staff checked the public address system before opening the hall for student orientation that morning.
examples.zh: 那天上午，大厅开放举行新生说明会之前，工作人员检查了「公共广播系统」。

words.enDefinition: A warning displayed on the screen of a computer.

examples.en: A desktop alert appeared while we were using the computers in the language lab.
examples.zh: 我们在语音实验室用电脑时，屏幕上弹出一条「电脑桌面警报」。

examples.en: The desktop alert included the same closure information as the text on my phone.
examples.zh: 「电脑桌面警报」和我手机上的短信提供了相同的闭馆信息。

words.enDefinition: A web page that provides official updates and notices about an emergency.

examples.en: The emergency information page showed which buildings had reopened after the facilities team finished checking them.
examples.zh: 「紧急情况信息页」列出了设施管理团队检查完毕后已重新开放的楼宇。

examples.en: I bookmarked the emergency information page because it listed notices for all three campuses.
examples.zh: 我收藏了「紧急情况信息页」，因为它列出了三个校区的通知。

collocations: link to the emergency information page

words.enDefinition: A prominent strip on a website or screen that displays a warning.

examples.en: An alert banner appeared above the library hours on the university website this morning.
examples.zh: 今天早上，大学网站上图书馆开放时间的上方出现了「警报横幅」。

examples.en: The alert banner was still visible when I opened the page on my phone.
examples.zh: 我用手机打开页面时，仍然能看到「警报横幅」。

words.enDefinition: New information released by the institution responsible for communicating about an event.

examples.en: The official update posted at noon confirmed that the science building had reopened already.
examples.zh: 中午发布的「官方通报」确认理科楼已经重新开放。

examples.en: I checked for an official update after classmates shared different times for the reopening.
examples.zh: 同学们转发的重新开放时间各不相同，于是我去查看是否有「官方通报」。

words.enDefinition: An official signal that an emergency or its restrictions have ended.

examples.en: The library stayed closed until staff received the all clear from campus safety that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，图书馆一直关闭，直到工作人员收到校园安全部门的「警报解除通知」。

examples.en: Our group saw the all clear on the campus website before the text message arrived.
examples.zh: 短信还没到，我们小组就在校园网站上看到了「警报解除通知」。

words.enDefinition: To send out an official warning to the people affected.

examples.en: The university issued an alert about the building closure just before the afternoon classes started.
examples.zh: 下午的课刚要开始，大学就针对楼宇关闭一事「发布了警报」。

examples.en: The campus can issue an alert through the same system it uses for routine tests.
examples.zh: 学校可以用平时做例行测试的同一个系统「发布警报」。

collocations: issue an alert about a closure

words.enDefinition: To officially end a warning that was in effect.

examples.en: Campus safety lifted the alert after facilities staff confirmed the rooms were ready to reopen.
examples.zh: 设施管理人员确认各房间可以开放后，校园安全部门「解除了警报」。

examples.en: When they lifted the alert, a second message confirmed that the campus center was open.
examples.zh: 「解除警报」时，第二条消息确认了学生活动中心已开放。

collocations: lift an alert after an inspection
lift an alert for one building

words.enDefinition: A person included in the group that receives a warning from a notification system.

examples.en: The alert recipients included staff from the library as well as students living on campus.
examples.zh: 「警报接收人」包括图书馆工作人员和住校学生。

examples.en: Each alert recipient got the same test message, regardless of their department or year group.
examples.zh: 无论院系或年级，每名「警报接收人」都收到了相同的测试消息。

words.enDefinition: The process of getting a warning message to the intended devices or people.

examples.en: The test helped staff notice a delay in alert delivery to some campus email accounts.
examples.zh: 这次测试让工作人员发现，向部分校园邮箱「投递警报」有延迟。

examples.en: The survey about alert delivery asked which device showed the notice first that morning.
examples.zh: 「警报投递」调查询问了那天早上哪台设备最先显示通知。

words.enDefinition: Settings that describe how someone wants to receive alerts, when choices are available.

examples.en: I checked my alert preferences after realizing the university still had my previous phone number.
examples.zh: 发现学校还存着我的旧号码后，我检查了自己的「警报接收偏好」。

examples.en: The orientation slideshow showed where to find alert preferences on the campus safety website.
examples.zh: 新生说明会的幻灯片展示了在校园安全网站的哪里可以找到「警报接收偏好」。

words.enDefinition: To register to receive safety warnings from a university or college.

examples.en: At orientation, the residence staff showed visitors where to sign up for campus alerts.
examples.zh: 新生说明会上，宿舍工作人员告诉访客去哪里「注册接收校园警报」。

examples.en: My tutor signed up for campus alerts after moving to the satellite campus this semester.
examples.zh: 导师本学期搬到分校区后，「注册接收了校园警报」。

collocations: sign up for campus alerts online
sign up for campus alerts by phone
help visitors sign up for campus alerts

words.enDefinition: A message sent to check whether a communication system is working.

examples.en: I got the test message during a seminar and recognized the label at once.
examples.zh: 研讨课上我收到了「测试消息」，一下就认出了它的标签。

examples.en: The test message showed up on my phone long before the copy in my inbox.
examples.zh: 手机上的「测试消息」比邮箱里的那份早到了很久。

words.enDefinition: A statement indicating that a message or alarm is part of a system check.

examples.en: The email started with “This is a test” above the name of the campus.
examples.zh: 邮件以「这是一次测试」开头，下方是校区名称。

examples.en: I heard “This is a test” over the speakers before the tone played again.
examples.zh: 提示音再次响起前，我听见扬声器里说「这是一次测试」。

collocations: a message headed this is a test
start with this is a test

words.enDefinition: A notice telling recipients that they do not need to do anything in response to the message.

examples.en: The test notification ended with “No action required” in bold letters below the heading.
examples.zh: 测试通知的末尾，在标题下方用粗体写着「无需采取行动」。

examples.en: The last line said “No action required” because this was a communications system check.
examples.zh: 最后一行写的是「无需采取行动」，因为这是一次通信系统检查。

collocations: a message saying no action required

words.enDefinition: A distinctive sound used to draw attention to an alert.

examples.en: The alert tone was distinct enough that I noticed it through the noise outside.
examples.zh: 「警报提示音」很特别，即使外面很吵我也听见了。

examples.en: We heard the alert tone just before a recorded announcement explained the system test.
examples.zh: 录音广播说明这次系统测试之前，我们听到了「警报提示音」。

words.enDefinition: A warning delivered as a sound that people can hear.

examples.en: The inspection form had a separate line for the audible warning and the flashing lights.
examples.zh: 检查表对「声音警报」和闪灯分别列了一项。

examples.en: The audible warning carried into the seminar room even though the door was already closed.
examples.zh: 虽然研讨室的门已经关上，「声音警报」仍然传了进去。

collocations: an audible warning in the corridor

words.enDefinition: A warning communicated through a visible display or flashing light.

examples.en: The visual warning was easy to see from the back of the crowded hall.
examples.zh: 在拥挤的大厅后排也很容易看到「视觉警报」。

examples.en: The accessibility guide showed what the visual warning looked like in the residence hallway.
examples.zh: 无障碍指南展示了宿舍走廊里的「视觉警报」是什么样子。

words.enDefinition: A spoken announcement saved in advance for later playback.

examples.en: We heard a recorded announcement explaining that the public address system was being tested.
examples.zh: 我们听到一条「预录广播」，说明公共广播系统正在测试。

examples.en: A recorded announcement gave the building name twice before the speakers went quiet again.
examples.zh: 扬声器再次安静前，「预录广播」把楼名重复了两遍。

collocations: a prerecorded announcement in the lobby

words.enDefinition: An official notice with information about safety issues affecting a campus community.

examples.en: The campus safety bulletin explained where students would see announcements about the upcoming fire drill.
examples.zh: 「校园安全简报」说明了学生可以在哪里看到即将举行的消防演习通知。

examples.en: Each campus safety bulletin was dated so students could tell which one was current.
examples.zh: 每份「校园安全简报」都注明了日期，学生可以分辨哪份是最新的。

collocations: a campus safety bulletin about drills

words.enDefinition: A warning intended for the entire campus community, across departments or buildings.

examples.en: The campus-wide alert appeared on screens in the gym and both of the student centers.
examples.zh: 「全校警报」显示在体育馆和两个学生中心的屏幕上。

examples.en: The campus-wide alert reached my roommate even though she was studying off campus that morning.
examples.zh: 虽然室友那天上午在校外学习，她也收到了「全校警报」。

words.enDefinition: An official written announcement giving essential information about an emergency.

examples.en: An emergency notice on the library door listed the closed areas and a time for the next update.
examples.zh: 图书馆门上的「紧急通告」列出了关闭区域和下次更新的时间。

examples.en: The emergency notice on the website included a short statement from the facilities team.
examples.zh: 网站上的「紧急通告」包含设施管理团队的一份简短说明。

collocations: an emergency notice on the door

words.enDefinition: A status label indicating that an incident has been addressed.

examples.en: The notification changed to “Incident resolved” shortly before classes resumed in the arts building.
examples.zh: 艺术楼恢复上课前不久，通知状态变成了「事件已处理完毕」。

examples.en: I saw “Incident resolved” beside the library notice when I refreshed the page later.
examples.zh: 后来我刷新页面时，在图书馆通告旁看到了「事件已处理完毕」。

collocations: an incident was resolved at noon

words.enDefinition: A signal that warns occupants of a possible fire in a building.

examples.en: The fire alarm sounded during open studio hours, and the instructor paused our session.
examples.zh: 开放工作室期间响起了「火灾警报」，老师暂停了我们的活动。

examples.en: A notice at reception explained that the fire alarm would be tested on Wednesday.
examples.zh: 接待处的告示说明，星期三会测试「火灾警报」。

words.enDefinition: A panel that displays the status of a building's fire alarm system.

examples.en: The caretaker showed our orientation group the fire alarm panel beside the reception desk.
examples.zh: 管理员给我们新生小组看了接待台旁的「火灾报警控制面板」。

examples.en: Facilities staff checked the fire alarm panel while the student center was still closed.
examples.zh: 学生活动中心还没开放时，设施管理人员检查了「火灾报警控制面板」。

collocations: an indicator on the fire alarm panel

words.enDefinition: A wall-mounted device with a handle for manually signaling a fire alarm.

examples.en: The orientation guide included a picture of a fire alarm pull station in the lobby.
examples.zh: 新生指南里有一张大厅内「手拉式火灾报警装置」的照片。

examples.en: On our tour, the guide identified a fire alarm pull station near the stairwell.
examples.zh: 参观时，向导指明了楼梯间附近的「手拉式火灾报警装置」。

collocations: label a fire alarm pull station
a fire alarm pull station by the exit
inspect a fire alarm pull station

words.enDefinition: a device, often with a push panel in the UK, used to trigger a building fire alarm

examples.en: The UK campus map marked the fire alarm call point beside the stairwell door.
examples.zh: 英国这所大学的校园地图在楼梯间门旁标出了「手动火灾报警点」。

examples.en: I recognised the red fire alarm call point from a photograph in our orientation guide.
examples.zh: 我从迎新指南的一张照片里认出了红色的「手动火灾报警点」。

collocations: mark the fire alarm call point
a fire alarm call point on the wall
identify a fire alarm call point

words.enDefinition: A device that flashes repeatedly to give a visible warning.

examples.en: During the demo, we could see the strobe light from the end of the corridor.
examples.zh: 演示时，我们在走廊尽头就能看见「频闪警示灯」。

examples.en: The accessibility review noted that a shelf partly blocked the view of the strobe light.
examples.zh: 无障碍检查记录指出，一个架子遮住了部分「频闪警示灯」。

words.enDefinition: A device that sounds a loud warning when an alarm is active.

examples.en: The alarm horn was audible in the courtyard during the evening test at the library.
examples.zh: 傍晚图书馆做测试时，庭院里能听见「报警喇叭」。

examples.en: The facilities team put the alarm horn and the warning lights on separate inspection lists.
examples.zh: 设施管理团队将「报警喇叭」和警示灯分别列在两张检查清单上。

words.enDefinition: A description of an alarm starting to sound or signal.

examples.en: The classroom falls quiet whenever the alarm goes off during the monthly equipment test.
examples.zh: 每月设备测试中一「响起警报」，教室里就立刻安静下来。

examples.en: I was signing in at reception when the alarm went off for the scheduled test.
examples.zh: 我正在接待处签到，这时例行测试的「警报响了」。

collocations: the alarm went off during class

words.enDefinition: An alarm that signals danger when there is no active danger in the situation.

examples.en: The campus update called it a false alarm after staff checked the lecture halls.
examples.zh: 工作人员检查阶梯教室后，校园通报称这是一次「误报」。

examples.en: It took a few minutes for the residence team to confirm the false alarm.
examples.zh: 宿舍管理团队花了几分钟才确认是「误报」。

collocations: a report of a false alarm

words.enDefinition: An alarm system that uses one signal to warn occupants and another to signal evacuation.

examples.en: The safety officer explained the two-stage alarm during orientation in the performing arts building.
examples.zh: 安全负责人在表演艺术楼的新生说明会上讲解了「两阶段警报」。

examples.en: The video used different colors to show the two signals of the two-stage alarm.
examples.zh: 视频用了不同颜色展示「两阶段警报」的两种信号。

collocations: a building with a two-stage alarm

words.enDefinition: A planned check of whether an alarm system functions.

examples.en: The day of the alarm test was listed on the noticeboard beside our mailboxes.
examples.zh: 「警报测试」的日期写在我们信箱旁的告示板上。

examples.en: My supervisor moved our meeting because an alarm test was scheduled for the same time.
examples.zh: 由于同时安排了「警报测试」，导师改了我们的会议时间。

words.enDefinition: A network of devices that releases water when appropriate fire conditions are detected.

examples.en: The fire sprinkler system at the library was listed in the facilities inspection summary.
examples.zh: 图书馆的「自动喷水灭火系统」列在设施检查摘要中。

examples.en: The tour explained why the new dormitory included a fire sprinkler system on every floor.
examples.zh: 参观时，向导解释了新宿舍每层都设有「自动喷水灭火系统」的原因。

collocations: a building with a fire sprinkler system

words.enDefinition: The individual fitting through which water is released in a fire sprinkler system.

examples.en: The maintenance request included a picture of a damaged sprinkler head in the study lounge.
examples.zh: 维修申请附了一张自习室里损坏的「消防喷头」的照片。

examples.en: A label next to each sprinkler head was visible in the model of the residence.
examples.zh: 宿舍模型里，每个「消防喷头」旁边的标签都看得见。

collocations: a sprinkler head in the ceiling

words.enDefinition: A portable device designed to put out a small fire.

examples.en: A campus map marked the fire extinguisher beside the main entrance to the ceramics studio.
examples.zh: 校园地图标出了陶艺工作室正门旁的「灭火器」。

examples.en: The facilities team checked the tag on each fire extinguisher in the residence hall.
examples.zh: 设施管理团队检查了宿舍楼里每个「灭火器」上的标签。

words.enDefinition: A wall cabinet that houses a fire extinguisher.

examples.en: The fire extinguisher cabinet stood out clearly against the pale wall near the snack machines.
examples.zh: 零食售货机附近，浅色墙上的「灭火器箱」特别显眼。

examples.en: The housing team replaced the cracked glass on the fire extinguisher cabinet in our hallway.
examples.zh: 宿舍管理团队换掉了我们走廊里「灭火器箱」上开裂的玻璃。

words.enDefinition: A piece of fire-resistant material intended to cover a small fire.

examples.en: The studio inventory included a fire blanket near the sink and one by the door.
examples.zh: 工作室的物品清单上，水槽旁和门边各有一条「灭火毯」。

examples.en: The residence handbook had a photograph of the fire blanket in the shared kitchen.
examples.zh: 宿舍手册里有一张公共厨房内「灭火毯」的照片。

collocations: a fire blanket in the lab

words.enDefinition: A device that detects a high temperature or a rapid rise in temperature as a sign of fire.

examples.en: The building inventory listed a heat detector inside the kitchenette on the basement floor.
examples.zh: 楼宇设备清单上，地下层的小厨房内有一个「感温探测器」。

examples.en: The lab manager identified the heat detector on the ceiling when our group toured the facility.
examples.zh: 我们小组参观设施时，实验室管理员指认了天花板上的「感温探测器」。

collocations: a heat detector in the kitchen

words.enDefinition: A device that warns people when it detects a dangerous amount of carbon monoxide.

examples.en: The residence checklist listed a carbon monoxide alarm in the corridor near the boiler room.
examples.zh: 宿舍检查清单列出了锅炉房附近走廊里的「一氧化碳报警器」。

examples.en: The housing office confirmed a carbon monoxide alarm had been checked during the previous inspection.
examples.zh: 宿舍管理处确认，上次检查时已经查验过「一氧化碳报警器」。

collocations: a carbon monoxide alarm in the hallway

words.enDefinition: A door designed to limit the spread of fire and smoke between spaces.

examples.en: A sticker identified the heavy door near the downstairs stairwell as a fire door.
examples.zh: 楼下楼梯间附近那扇厚重的门上贴着标签，注明是「防火门」。

examples.en: We saw a fire door on the campus safety tour of the new theater.
examples.zh: 我们参加新剧院的校园安全参观时，看到了一扇「防火门」。

words.enDefinition: A sign indicating that a fire door is meant to stay closed.

examples.en: The notice on the workshop door said “Fire door keep shut” above the handle.
examples.zh: 工作间的门把手上方贴着「防火门请保持关闭」的告示。

examples.en: The student handbook showed a photograph with the words “Fire door keep shut” clearly visible.
examples.zh: 学生手册里的照片上清楚地写着「防火门请保持关闭」。

collocations: a fire door keep shut sign
a label reading fire door keep shut

words.enDefinition: Lighting that provides illumination when the normal lighting fails.

examples.en: Facilities staff tested the emergency lighting while the hall was empty on Friday morning.
examples.zh: 星期五早上大厅空着时，设施管理人员测试了「应急照明」。

examples.en: The emergency lighting in the stairwell made the steps visible during the maintenance check.
examples.zh: 维护检查期间，楼梯间的「应急照明」照亮了台阶。

words.enDefinition: A designated exit for leaving a place in an emergency.

examples.en: The tour guide pointed out the emergency exit at the back of the rehearsal room.
examples.zh: 参观向导指给我们看排练室后方的「紧急出口」。

examples.en: Our floor map showed an emergency exit at each end of the long corridor.
examples.zh: 楼层图上显示，长走廊两端各有一个「紧急出口」。

words.enDefinition: A label indicating that an exit is reserved for emergency use.

examples.en: The door nearest our seats was marked “Emergency exit only” in large white letters.
examples.zh: 离座位最近的门上用醒目的白字写着「仅供紧急疏散使用」。

examples.en: The lobby diagram used a separate symbol for each door marked “Emergency exit only” upstairs.
examples.zh: 大厅平面图用了单独的符号标识楼上写有「仅供紧急疏散使用」的每扇门。

collocations: mark a door emergency exit only
a door labeled emergency exit only

words.enDefinition: A sign warning that using a particular door or device will cause an alarm.

examples.en: The door had a small label reading “Alarm will sound” just below the handle.
examples.zh: 那扇门把手正下方贴有一张小标签，上面写着「将触发警报」。

examples.en: I noticed “Alarm will sound” printed under the exit symbol on the workshop door.
examples.zh: 我发现工作室门上的出口图标下方印着「将触发警报」。

collocations: a label reading alarm will sound
an alarm will sound when opened

words.enDefinition: A notice directing people not to use a lift under the conditions stated on the sign.

examples.en: The poster said “Do not use the lift” below a symbol of a flame.
examples.zh: 海报上火焰图标下方写着「请勿使用电梯」。

examples.en: We translated “Do not use the lift” from a sample building notice during orientation.
examples.zh: 新生说明会上，我们翻译了楼宇示例告示中的「请勿使用电梯」。

collocations: a sign reading do not use the lift
a do not use the lift notice
do not use the lift during a fire

words.enDefinition: A posted notice describing a building's procedures in the event of a fire.

examples.en: I saw the fire action notice while waiting for my room keys at reception.
examples.zh: 在接待台等着领房间钥匙时，我看到了「火灾应对告示」。

examples.en: The fire action notice in our seminar room identified the assembly point in bold type.
examples.zh: 我们研讨室里的「火灾应对告示」用粗体标出了集合点。

collocations: a fire action notice near the stairs

words.enDefinition: A stairwell identified as part of a building's emergency exit route.

examples.en: The emergency stairwell was shown in green on the plan beside the auditorium doors.
examples.zh: 礼堂门旁的平面图用绿色标出了「应急楼梯间」。

examples.en: Our building tour ended in the lobby next to the sign for the emergency stairwell.
examples.zh: 楼宇参观在大厅结束，旁边就是「应急楼梯间」的指示牌。

collocations: a door to the emergency stairwell

words.enDefinition: A marked lane kept open for fire service vehicles to reach a building.

examples.en: The fire lane was marked in red outside the entrance to our residence hall.
examples.zh: 我们宿舍楼入口外的「消防通道」用红色标出。

examples.en: A sign identified the narrow driveway beside the service entrance as a fire lane.
examples.zh: 一块标牌注明，后勤入口旁的狭窄车道是「消防通道」。

words.enDefinition: Equipment intended to detect, warn about, or help control a fire.

examples.en: The campus fire safety equipment shown in the booklet included alarms and a fire blanket.
examples.zh: 手册上展示的校园「消防设备」包括报警器和灭火毯。

examples.en: A facilities employee updated the inspection list for the fire safety equipment in our building.
examples.zh: 一名设施管理人员更新了我们楼内「消防设备」的检查清单。

words.enDefinition: A review of a location and its equipment for fire safety conditions.

examples.en: The fire safety inspection started after the last group finished using the rehearsal rooms.
examples.zh: 最后一组用完排练室后，开始了「消防安全检查」。

examples.en: A fire safety inspection report listed the dates for repairs to several damaged signs.
examples.zh: 「消防安全检查」报告列出了几块损坏告示牌的维修日期。

words.enDefinition: A condition or object that increases the risk of a fire or makes it more dangerous.

examples.en: The inspection report identified the damaged cable under the table as a potential fire hazard.
examples.zh: 检查报告将桌下那根破损电线认定为一处潜在的「火灾隐患」。

examples.en: Our residence orientation included photos to show what staff meant by a fire hazard.
examples.zh: 宿舍说明会用了几张照片来说明工作人员所说的「火灾隐患」指什么。

words.enDefinition: To leave a place because conditions are unsafe or may become unsafe.

examples.en: The announcement explained why we had to evacuate halfway through the afternoon study session.
examples.zh: 广播解释了为什么我们下午自习到一半就得「疏散」。

examples.en: Our group practiced how to evacuate during a scheduled exercise at the student center.
examples.zh: 我们小组在学生活动中心的例行演练中练习了如何「疏散」。

words.enDefinition: An official instruction requiring the people in a specified place to leave.

examples.en: The notice included an evacuation order for the main library and the attached offices.
examples.zh: 通知中包含针对主图书馆及相连办公室的「疏散令」。

examples.en: The university lifted the evacuation order and posted a separate update about the reading rooms.
examples.zh: 大学撤销了「疏散令」，并单独发布了一条关于阅览室的通报。

collocations: an evacuation order for one building

words.enDefinition: A signal indicating that people are expected to leave a building or area.

examples.en: We heard the evacuation alarm during the afternoon rehearsal for the campus safety exercise.
examples.zh: 下午校园安全演习预演时，我们听到了「疏散警报」。

examples.en: The video played a sample of the evacuation alarm used in the student residences.
examples.zh: 视频播放了学生宿舍所用「疏散警报」的样音。

words.enDefinition: The established steps for leaving a place safely during an emergency.

examples.en: The residence handbook explained the evacuation procedure before listing the building's quiet hours and guest rules.
examples.zh: 宿舍手册先介绍「疏散程序」，再列出楼内的安静时段和访客规则。

examples.en: Our tutor reviewed the evacuation procedure when the seminar moved to a different building.
examples.zh: 研讨课换到另一栋楼后，导师带我们复习了「疏散程序」。

words.enDefinition: A planned path for leaving a building or area during an emergency.

examples.en: The map on the wall showed the evacuation route from our floor to the courtyard.
examples.zh: 墙上的地图标出了从我们所在楼层通往庭院的「疏散路线」。

examples.en: We noticed the evacuation route changed after the hall reopened with a new entrance.
examples.zh: 大厅启用新入口重新开放后，我们发现「疏散路线」变了。

words.enDefinition: Another exit that can be used if the usual exit is unavailable.

examples.en: The floor plan showed an alternative exit next to the lockers near the rear entrance.
examples.zh: 楼层图显示，后门附近的储物柜旁有一个「备用出口」。

examples.en: The guide circled an alternative exit on the map during our tour of the theater.
examples.zh: 参观剧院时，向导在地图上圈出了一个「备用出口」。

collocations: an alternative exit from the hall

words.enDefinition: An exit that cannot be used freely because something is in the way.

examples.en: The residence staff moved the boxes after a student reported a blocked exit upstairs.
examples.zh: 一名学生报告楼上有个「被堵塞的出口」后，宿舍工作人员搬走了箱子。

examples.en: There was a photo of a blocked exit on the facilities team's safety checklist.
examples.zh: 设施管理团队的安全检查清单上有一张「被堵塞的出口」的照片。

collocations: a complaint about a blocked exit

words.enDefinition: A continuous path that lets occupants leave a building and reach a safe outside area.

examples.en: The facilities diagram used the term “means of egress” for the route leading outside.
examples.zh: 设施示意图把通往室外的路线标成了「安全疏散通道」。

examples.en: The campus planner highlighted the means of egress on a copy of the building plan.
examples.zh: 校园规划人员在楼宇平面图的复印件上标出了「安全疏散通道」。

collocations: a means of egress from the building

words.enDefinition: A diagram showing routes, exits, or other locations relevant to leaving a building in an emergency.

examples.en: The evacuation map near the lift showed the exits on our floor in green.
examples.zh: 电梯旁的「疏散示意图」用绿色标明了我们这层楼的出口。

examples.en: The school replaced the evacuation map after the old reception area was turned into classrooms.
examples.zh: 原来的接待区改成教室后，学校换了新的「疏散示意图」。

collocations: an evacuation map for the floor

words.enDefinition: A designated location where people gather after leaving a building in an emergency.

examples.en: The assembly point for this wing was marked on the map beside the studio door.
examples.zh: 工作室门旁的地图标出了这片楼区的「疏散集合点」。

examples.en: The guide pointed out the assembly point as we walked past the open sports field.
examples.zh: 路过露天运动场时，向导指给我们看「疏散集合点」。

collocations: a sign for the assembly point

words.enDefinition: To verify where everyone in a group is after an evacuation or other event.

examples.en: The hall staff compared two lists to account for everyone after the practice evacuation.
examples.zh: 疏散练习结束后，宿舍工作人员对照两份名单「确认了每个人的去向」。

examples.en: Our supervisor wanted to account for everyone before the exercise was officially declared over.
examples.zh: 在演习正式宣布结束前，我们的主管想「确认每个人的去向」。

collocations: make sure you can account for everyone
account for everyone on the list
account for everyone after the drill

words.enDefinition: To go to the designated gathering place so your presence can be checked.

examples.en: During the exercise, the recording asked residents to report to the assembly point outside.
examples.zh: 演习期间，录音广播请住户「到室外集合点报到」。

examples.en: We learned which path to take when asked to report to the assembly point.
examples.zh: 我们了解了在被要求「到集合点报到」时应走哪条路。

collocations: report to the assembly point outside
report to your assigned assembly point
be asked to report to the assembly point

words.enDefinition: Describes people whose whereabouts have not yet been verified.

examples.en: The warden said two visitors were unaccounted for until the reception team checked the register.
examples.zh: 疏散负责人说，接待团队核查登记册之前，有两名访客「去向尚未确认」。

examples.en: It turned out that the student marked as unaccounted for had already left for class.
examples.zh: 后来发现，标记为「去向尚未确认」的那名学生已经去上课了。

words.enDefinition: A systematic check of the spaces in a building during a drill or evacuation.

examples.en: The drill observer noted when the building sweep was complete on the evaluation form.
examples.zh: 演习观察员在评估表上记录了「楼内逐区检查」的完成时间。

examples.en: The staff briefing explained which teams were responsible for the building sweep during the exercise.
examples.zh: 工作人员简报解释了演习时哪些小组负责「楼内逐区检查」。

collocations: a building sweep during a drill
record the time of a building sweep

words.enDefinition: People who are inside a building at a given time.

examples.en: The notice informed building occupants that the scheduled alarm test had been moved to Friday.
examples.zh: 告示通知「楼内人员」，原定的警报测试已改到星期五。

examples.en: The exercise form asked how many building occupants had reached the assembly point by noon.
examples.zh: 演习表询问，截至中午有多少「楼内人员」到达了集合点。

words.enDefinition: A designated person who helps coordinate an evacuation for a building or area.

examples.en: The evacuation warden wore a labeled vest throughout the drill at the student union.
examples.zh: 学生活动中心演习期间，「疏散负责人」全程穿着带标识的背心。

examples.en: Our new staff guide listed the evacuation warden for every floor of the building.
examples.zh: 我们的新员工指南列出了楼内每一层的「疏散负责人」。

words.enDefinition: A person assigned to coordinate emergency procedures for a particular floor.

examples.en: The floor warden joined our class briefly to explain what the drill would sound like.
examples.zh: 「楼层安全负责人」来我们班简单说了演习时会听到什么声音。

examples.en: The list outside the stairwell identified the floor warden assigned to the computer labs.
examples.zh: 楼梯间外的名单注明了负责机房的「楼层安全负责人」。

collocations: floor warden for the second floor

words.enDefinition: Help provided to someone who needs support to leave a building in an emergency.

examples.en: A student asked about evacuation assistance before booking a room for the evening workshop.
examples.zh: 一名学生为晚间研讨活动订房间前，询问了「疏散协助」的安排。

examples.en: The accessibility guide explained what evacuation assistance was available during events in the auditorium.
examples.zh: 无障碍指南说明了在礼堂举办活动时可获得哪些「疏散协助」。

words.enDefinition: A designated protected space where someone can wait for evacuation assistance.

examples.en: The floor map marked an area of refuge near the stairwell on each upper level.
examples.zh: 楼层图标出了楼上每层楼梯间附近的「避难等候区」。

examples.en: Our tour guide paused outside the area of refuge to explain what the sign meant.
examples.zh: 向导在「避难等候区」外停下来讲解标志的含义。

collocations: signs for the area of refuge

words.enDefinition: An intercom that allows someone in an area of refuge to communicate with staff.

examples.en: A yellow symbol on the accessibility map marked the refuge intercom on the upper floor.
examples.zh: 无障碍地图上的黄色图标标出了楼上的「避难区对讲装置」。

examples.en: Facilities staff recorded the date of the refuge intercom test on the inspection sheet.
examples.zh: 设施管理人员在检查表上记下了「避难区对讲装置」的测试日期。

collocations: a refuge intercom at the stairwell

words.enDefinition: A specialized chair designed to help trained people move someone who cannot use stairs independently.

examples.en: The building guide showed the location of an evacuation chair on the second floor.
examples.zh: 楼宇指南标明了二楼一把「疏散椅」的位置。

examples.en: An evacuation chair was shown in the diagram next to the building's accessibility features.
examples.zh: 楼宇无障碍设施旁的示意图里画有一把「疏散椅」。

words.enDefinition: An evacuation plan tailored to the support needs of an individual person.

examples.en: The student met with accessibility staff to discuss a personal emergency evacuation plan before classes began.
examples.zh: 这名学生开课前与无障碍服务人员讨论了「个人应急疏散计划」。

examples.en: The advisor reviewed her personal emergency evacuation plan after the department moved to another building.
examples.zh: 院系搬到另一栋楼后，顾问重新审看了她的「个人应急疏散计划」。

collocations: prepare a personal emergency evacuation plan
review a personal emergency evacuation plan
discuss a personal emergency evacuation plan

words.enDefinition: An emergency exit route designed to be usable by people with accessibility needs.

examples.en: The accessibility map showed an accessible evacuation route starting at the back of the auditorium.
examples.zh: 无障碍地图上标出了一条从礼堂后部开始的「无障碍疏散路线」。

examples.en: Our group asked whether the accessible evacuation route had changed after the lobby was renovated.
examples.zh: 我们小组询问，大厅翻新后「无障碍疏散路线」是否变了。

collocations: an accessible evacuation route on a floor plan

words.enDefinition: A lift specifically designed and designated for use as part of a building evacuation plan.

examples.en: The building plan marked the evacuation lift separately from the regular lifts in the lobby.
examples.zh: 楼宇平面图把「疏散电梯」与大厅里的普通电梯分别标出。

examples.en: Our campus tour guide explained why the new building had a separate evacuation lift.
examples.zh: 校园参观的向导解释了新楼为什么配有单独的「疏散电梯」。

collocations: an evacuation lift in the floor plan

words.enDefinition: An evacuation in which a person receives help to leave safely.

examples.en: The drill report recorded how long the assisted evacuation took in the older residence hall.
examples.zh: 演练报告记录了旧宿舍楼内「有人协助的疏散」用了多长时间。

examples.en: The floor warden checked that staff were available for an assisted evacuation that evening.
examples.zh: 楼层安全负责人确认，当晚有工作人员可以配合「有人协助的疏散」。

collocations: an assisted evacuation during a drill

words.enDefinition: To leave a place in an emergency without assistance from other people.

examples.en: The planning form asked whether each participant would be able to self-evacuate from that room.
examples.zh: 计划表询问每位参与者能否从那间房「自行疏散」。

examples.en: Staff discussed how they would support students who might be unable to self-evacuate from upstairs.
examples.zh: 工作人员讨论了如何支持可能无法从楼上「自行疏散」的学生。

words.enDefinition: An exit that can be reached without having to use steps.

examples.en: The doorway on the north side was labeled as the step-free exit on the event map.
examples.zh: 活动地图把北侧门口标为「无台阶出口」。

examples.en: We could see the sign for the step-free exit from the entrance to the lecture hall.
examples.zh: 从阶梯教室入口可以看到「无台阶出口」的指示牌。

collocations: a step-free exit to the street

words.enDefinition: To go into a building again after leaving it.

examples.en: We were allowed to re-enter the building after the practice session ended and staff finished their checks.
examples.zh: 演习结束且工作人员完成检查后，我们获准「重新进入楼内」。

examples.en: I asked at the desk when we could re-enter the building to collect our bags.
examples.zh: 我在服务台询问什么时候可以「重新进入楼内」取包。

collocations: be allowed to re-enter the building

words.enDefinition: To stay inside a building or designated place temporarily for protection.

examples.en: Our group discussed what “shelter in place” meant when reading an example campus alert.
examples.zh: 阅读校园警报示例时，我们小组讨论了「就地避险」的含义。

examples.en: The safety video used the phrase “shelter in place” in a sample announcement.
examples.zh: 安全视频中，一条例示广播用了「就地避险」这个说法。

collocations: an instruction to shelter in place
be asked to shelter in place
a notice to shelter in place

words.enDefinition: A practice exercise for responding to a fire alarm, often including evacuation.

examples.en: We had a fire drill on the first morning of the summer language course.
examples.zh: 暑期语言课程的第一天上午，我们参加了「消防演习」。

examples.en: The residence staff discussed the fire drill at our meeting in the common room.
examples.zh: 宿舍工作人员在公共休息室的会议上谈到了「消防演习」。

collocations: take part in a fire drill

words.enDefinition: A notice telling people that a practice exercise is planned or underway.

examples.en: A drill notice appeared next to the printer at the start of the week.
examples.zh: 周初，打印机旁贴出一份「演习通知」。

examples.en: The drill notice listed both the start time and the buildings involved in the exercise.
examples.zh: 「演习通知」列出了演习开始时间和涉及的楼宇。

collocations: a drill notice on the noticeboard

words.enDefinition: A practice exercise whose exact timing is not announced to participants in advance.

examples.en: The report described an unannounced drill that took place during a regular afternoon class.
examples.zh: 报告介绍了一次在下午正常上课时举行的「未提前通知的演习」。

examples.en: The residence handbook explained what the staff meant by an unannounced drill for new students.
examples.zh: 宿舍手册向新生解释了工作人员所说的「未提前通知的演习」是什么。

words.enDefinition: Planning and training done in advance to be ready for emergencies.

examples.en: The university added a short session on emergency preparedness to orientation week this year.
examples.zh: 今年，大学在迎新周增加了一节简短的「应急准备」课程。

examples.en: Our residence meeting covered emergency preparedness and explained where safety notices were usually posted.
examples.zh: 宿舍会议讲到了「应急准备」，还说明了安全通告通常贴在哪里。

words.enDefinition: A document laying out responsibilities and procedures to follow during an emergency.

examples.en: The building manager shared the emergency action plan with departments that had recently moved in.
examples.zh: 楼宇管理员把「应急行动计划」发给了刚搬进来的各个部门。

examples.en: A copy of the emergency action plan was available at reception for staff and visitors.
examples.zh: 接待处备有一份「应急行动计划」，供工作人员和访客查阅。

words.enDefinition: A discussion-based exercise in which participants talk through responses to a simulated situation.

examples.en: The residence staff held a tabletop exercise to discuss a fictional building closure during exams.
examples.zh: 宿舍工作人员举行了一次「桌面推演」，讨论考试期间某栋楼虚构的关闭情境。

examples.en: At the tabletop exercise, each department explained what information it would need from campus management.
examples.zh: 「桌面推演」中，各部门说明了需要校园管理部门提供哪些信息。

collocations: take part in a tabletop exercise

words.enDefinition: A person assigned to watch and record what happens during a practice exercise.

examples.en: The drill observer wrote down which signs the new students noticed in the main lobby.
examples.zh: 「演习观察员」记下了新生在主大厅里留意到哪些告示。

examples.en: Each drill observer handed in a short form before the staff meeting the next day.
examples.zh: 次日的员工会议开始前，每位「演习观察员」都交了一张简短的表格。

words.enDefinition: A discussion after a practice exercise to review what happened and what might be improved.

examples.en: During the drill debrief, students said the announcement was clearer in the hallway than outside.
examples.zh: 在「演习复盘」中，学生说走廊里的广播比室外的清楚。

examples.en: The building manager invited reception staff to the drill debrief after the morning exercise.
examples.zh: 上午演习结束后，楼宇管理员请接待处工作人员参加「演习复盘」。

words.enDefinition: A label indicating that a practice exercise is currently underway.

examples.en: A sign reading “Drill in progress” stood outside the reception doors during our tour.
examples.zh: 我们参观时，接待处门外立着一块写有「演习进行中」的牌子。

examples.en: The welcome desk put out “Drill in progress” signs before the first group arrived.
examples.zh: 第一组抵达前，迎宾服务台摆出了写有「演习进行中」的牌子。

collocations: a notice marked drill in progress

words.enDefinition: A check of a system arranged in advance for a particular time.

examples.en: The university mentioned the scheduled system test in its newsletter two days before the event.
examples.zh: 大学在测试开始两天前的简报里提到了「预定的系统测试」。

examples.en: I received a text marked “Scheduled system test” while studying in the media room.
examples.zh: 我在媒体室学习时收到一条标有「预定的系统测试」的短信。

words.enDefinition: An organized activity used to practice or evaluate how people respond to an emergency.

examples.en: Several departments took part in the emergency exercise before the new residence opened to students.
examples.zh: 新宿舍向学生开放前，几个部门参加了「应急演练」。

examples.en: Our tutor used an emergency exercise to show how the faculty communicates during disruptions.
examples.zh: 导师用一次「应急演练」展示了院系在运营中断期间如何传递信息。

collocations: take part in an emergency exercise

words.enDefinition: The amount of time people take to leave a place during an evacuation or drill.

examples.en: The observer recorded the evacuation time on a clipboard after our group reached the courtyard.
examples.zh: 我们小组到达庭院后，观察员在写字板上记录了「疏散用时」。

examples.en: The report compared the evacuation time for each floor during the two practice sessions.
examples.zh: 报告对比了两次练习中每层楼的「疏散用时」。

words.enDefinition: A period in which a building is closed to some or all of its usual users.

examples.en: The building closure affected two lectures and the language exchange meeting in the afternoon.
examples.zh: 「楼宇关闭」影响了下午的两节讲座和一场语言交流活动。

examples.en: The university posted a note about the building closure beside the regular opening hours.
examples.zh: 大学把「楼宇关闭」的通知贴在常规开放时间旁。

collocations: a notice about a building closure

words.enDefinition: To return to the usual running of an institution or facility after a disruption.

examples.en: The student center was able to resume normal operations after the inspection ended that afternoon.
examples.zh: 当天下午检查结束后，学生活动中心得以「恢复正常运营」。

examples.en: The email said both libraries would resume normal operations at their regular time on Monday.
examples.zh: 邮件说，两家图书馆将于星期一的常规时间「恢复正常运营」。

collocations: be ready to resume normal operations
a date to resume normal operations

words.enDefinition: The current condition of a place or service, such as open, closed, or limited.

examples.en: I checked the operating status of the library before leaving for my afternoon study session.
examples.zh: 去参加下午的自习活动前，我查看了图书馆的「运营状态」。

examples.en: The university's front page displayed the operating status of each facility in a short table.
examples.zh: 大学首页用一张简表显示了各设施的「运营状态」。

words.enDefinition: An announcement that previously suspended classes will restart.

examples.en: The department wrote that classes will resume on Tuesday in the usual lecture rooms.
examples.zh: 院系书面通知称，星期二「课程将在原来的阶梯教室恢复」。

examples.en: I checked my timetable after the university announced that classes will resume as scheduled.
examples.zh: 大学宣布「课程将按原时间表恢复」后，我查看了自己的课表。

words.enDefinition: A change to the place where a class is held.

examples.en: I saw the class relocation on the department noticeboard before leaving for the afternoon lecture.
examples.zh: 我动身去听下午的课之前，在院系告示板上看到了「上课地点变更」信息。

examples.en: The class relocation put our Friday seminar in the smaller room beside the library.
examples.zh: 这次「上课地点变更」把星期五的研讨课安排到了图书馆旁的小房间。

collocations: a notice about a class relocation

words.enDefinition: An arrangement allowing people back into a building under supervision or in assigned stages.

examples.en: The email described controlled re-entry for students who had left personal belongings inside the library.
examples.zh: 邮件说明了对有物品遗留在图书馆的学生实行的「有序重新入内」安排。

examples.en: During the exercise, staff practiced how to organize controlled re-entry for a large group.
examples.zh: 演习期间，工作人员练习了如何组织大批人员「有序重新入内」。

collocations: allow controlled re-entry after a drill

words.enDefinition: A temporary barrier or marked boundary around an area to limit entry.

examples.en: A temporary cordon marked the area around the entrance while staff inspected the overhead sign.
examples.zh: 工作人员检查上方的标牌时，入口周围用「临时警戒线」标了出来。

examples.en: The temporary cordon was removed before the afternoon program in the courtyard started again.
examples.zh: 庭院里的下午活动重新开始前，「临时警戒线」撤掉了。

collocations: a temporary cordon around the area

words.enDefinition: A notice stating that a facility or area is closed, sometimes giving the reason or duration.

examples.en: A closure notice was taped to the glass door before the morning study group arrived.
examples.zh: 早上的学习小组到达前，玻璃门上已贴出「关闭告示」。

examples.en: The closure notice gave a reopening date and listed another study space across campus.
examples.zh: 「关闭告示」给出了重新开放的日期，并列出了校园另一边的一个学习场所。

collocations: a closure notice on the door

words.enDefinition: The time a place is expected to open again after a closure.

examples.en: We checked the expected reopening time before deciding whether to wait for the library.
examples.zh: 决定是否等图书馆开放前，我们查看了「预计重新开放时间」。

examples.en: The expected reopening time was shown at the bottom of the notice beside the entrance.
examples.zh: 「预计重新开放时间」写在入口旁告示的底部。

words.enDefinition: A notice that a place is expected to reopen later than previously announced.

examples.en: The website displayed “Reopening delayed” above the study center's hours on the following morning.
examples.zh: 第二天早上，网站在学习中心的开放时间上方显示「重新开放延期」。

examples.en: The status message changed to “Reopening delayed” while we were waiting outside the hall.
examples.zh: 我们在大厅外等候时，状态消息改成了「重新开放延期」。

collocations: a message that says reopening delayed

words.enDefinition: A place set aside where people can stay safely during an incident or exercise.

examples.en: A sign outside the student center identified the courtyard as the designated safe area for the drill.
examples.zh: 学生活动中心外的标牌注明，庭院是这次演习的「指定安全区域」。

examples.en: The volunteer guide delivered water to a designated safe area after the classroom building closed.
examples.zh: 教学楼关闭后，志愿引导员把水送到了「指定安全区域」。

collocations: wait in a designated safe area
a map of the designated safe area

words.enDefinition: A short meeting or talk covering safety information for a place or activity.

examples.en: Visitors joined a short safety briefing before going into the photography studio for their tour.
examples.zh: 访客进入摄影工作室参观前，参加了一场简短的「安全说明会」。

examples.en: The activity leader included a map of the building in the safety briefing for new students.
examples.zh: 活动负责人在面向新生的「安全说明会」中附上了楼宇地图。

words.enDefinition: An evacuation that begins without unnecessary delay.

examples.en: The drill report credited the clear announcements for the prompt evacuation of the rehearsal room.
examples.zh: 演习报告将排练室的「及时疏散」归功于清楚的广播。

examples.en: The staff briefing discussed how better signs had helped with prompt evacuation during the exercise.
examples.zh: 工作人员简报讨论了改善后的标牌如何帮助大家在演习中「及时疏散」。

collocations: a prompt evacuation of the space

words.enDefinition: A label introducing the time when more official information is expected.

examples.en: The banner read “Next update at noon” underneath the announcement about the library closure.
examples.zh: 横幅在图书馆关闭通知下方显示「下次更新于中午」。

examples.en: Staff added “Next update at four” when they revised the notice on the building doors.
examples.zh: 工作人员修改楼门上的告示时，补上了「下次更新于四点」。

collocations: a notice saying next update at noon
a banner with next update at four
a message ending with next update at three

words.enDefinition: A way a safety message is delivered, such as text, email, or a loudspeaker.

examples.en: The orientation guide listed text messaging as one available notification channel for campus safety alerts.
examples.zh: 新生指南把短信列为校园警报可用的「通知渠道」之一。

examples.en: The campus tested each notification channel separately while students were using the main library.
examples.zh: 学生使用主图书馆期间，学校分别测试了每种「通知渠道」。

words.enDefinition: The work of preparing for and coordinating an institution's response to emergencies on its campus.

examples.en: The notice named campus emergency management as the office responsible for the upcoming drill.
examples.zh: 告示注明，「校园应急管理」办公室负责即将举行的演习。

examples.en: A campus emergency management staff member helped our group understand the wording on the alert.
examples.zh: 一名「校园应急管理」工作人员帮我们小组理解了警报上的措辞。

words.enDefinition: A spoken announcement telling people that a practice exercise is about to begin or is in progress.

examples.en: The drill announcement was barely audible from the back of the student dining hall.
examples.zh: 从学生餐厅后部几乎听不见「演习广播」。

examples.en: We heard the drill announcement during a pause in our group discussion that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，我们在小组讨论的间隙听见了「演习广播」。

words.enDefinition: Material that is capable of catching fire and burning.

examples.en: The safety inspection report identified the cardboard beside the doorway as a combustible material.
examples.zh: 消防安全检查报告将门口旁的纸板列为「可燃材料」。

examples.en: Our studio inventory listed several kinds of combustible material kept in the storage room.
examples.zh: 工作室的物品清单列出了储物间中存放的几种「可燃材料」。

words.enDefinition: A horizontal bar fitted across a door that releases the latch when pushed.

examples.en: The guide identified the push bar across the emergency exit door in the auditorium.
examples.zh: 向导指给我们看了礼堂紧急出口门上的「出口门推杆」。

examples.en: The maintenance sheet listed a loose push bar on the door near the lobby.
examples.zh: 维修单注明，大厅附近的门上有一根松动的「出口门推杆」。

collocations: a door with a push bar
a push bar on an exit door

words.enDefinition: An area identified as a separate section in an evacuation plan or notice.

examples.en: The diagram marked each evacuation zone in a different color for the upcoming exercise.
examples.zh: 为即将举行的演习，示意图用不同颜色标出了每个「疏散分区」。

examples.en: Staff confirmed that the south corridor belonged to a different evacuation zone from the lobby.
examples.zh: 工作人员确认，南走廊与大厅属于不同的「疏散分区」。

collocations: an evacuation zone on the map

words.enDefinition: A label introducing the time when an official notice was released.

examples.en: The alert was marked “Issued at nine” near the top of the email message.
examples.zh: 警报邮件顶部附近标有「发布于九点」。

examples.en: The small line marked “Issued at” helped me identify the most recent notice on the page.
examples.zh: 「发布于」这一行小字帮助我分辨出页面上最新的通知。

collocations: an alert marked issued at noon
a notice with an issued at line

words.enDefinition: A fictional emergency presented as part of a training activity or exercise.

examples.en: Our classmates read the alert about the simulated emergency and discussed its wording in pairs.
examples.zh: 同学们读了关于「模拟紧急情况」的警报，然后两人一组讨论它的措辞。

examples.en: The simulated emergency was described in a handout before the practice exercise began that afternoon.
examples.zh: 当天下午练习开始前，讲义中介绍了这次「模拟紧急情况」。

collocations: a briefing about a simulated emergency

words.enDefinition: A marked vest that makes an evacuation warden easy to recognize.

examples.en: I recognized our floor warden by the yellow warden vest she wore during the exercise.
examples.zh: 演习时，我们楼层的负责人穿着黄色「疏散负责人识别背心」，我一下就认出了她。

examples.en: The training photo showed a warden vest with the building name printed on the back.
examples.zh: 培训照片里有一件「疏散负责人识别背心」，背面印着楼名。

collocations: identify someone by their warden vest

words.enDefinition: A wall or other building feature designed to limit the spread of smoke.

examples.en: The building diagram identified a smoke barrier between the rehearsal area and the main lobby.
examples.zh: 楼宇示意图标出了排练区与主大厅之间的「挡烟隔断」。

examples.en: The inspection summary listed the smoke barrier as a separate item under building safety features.
examples.zh: 检查摘要将「挡烟隔断」在楼宇安全设施下单独列为一项。

words.enDefinition: A message giving new information about an ongoing incident and its effects.

examples.en: The incident update added a list of rooms that were still unavailable that afternoon.
examples.zh: 「事件进展通报」补充了一份当天下午仍无法使用的房间清单。

examples.en: The next incident update explained when students could return to the ground floor study area.
examples.zh: 下一条「事件进展通报」说明了学生何时可以返回地面层自习区。

collocations: an incident update from campus management

words.enDefinition: An evacuation organized in stages for different building areas or groups.

examples.en: The staff briefing used a diagram to explain phased evacuation in the new auditorium.
examples.zh: 工作人员简报用一张示意图讲解了新礼堂的「分阶段疏散」。

examples.en: The training session covered phased evacuation and gave each observer a short evaluation form.
examples.zh: 培训课讲解了「分阶段疏散」，还给每位观察员发了一张简短的评估表。
